09:00.headline: Myth: only D1 has baseball money
09:00.topic: Myth-buster: athletic aid exists at D2, NAIA and many JUCO programs; D3 aid is academic and need-based
09:00.caption:
"If he's not D1, there's no baseball money."

We hear this from parents all the time. It isn't true, and believing it can shrink your player's list before it even starts.

⚾ D2 and NAIA programs can offer athletic aid.
⚾ Many JUCO programs can, too.
⚾ D3 schools don't give athletic scholarships, but academic and need-based aid can make them very affordable.

The better question isn't "Is it D1?" It's "Where does he fit, and what will it really cost us?" Compare the actual aid packages, not just the division.

Which level did you assume was out of reach? 👇

See what the numbers say about your player's best fit:

13:00.headline: Know his level before you email
13:00.topic: Know your level: 4-step order (numbers, compare by level, mixed list, email best-fit coaches first)
13:00.caption:
Is your player emailing coaches at schools where he doesn't fit yet?

It's one of the most common ways families lose a year. Before the next email goes out, try this order:

1️⃣ Get verified numbers: velo, exit velo, 60 time, pop time.
2️⃣ Compare them with typical ranges at D1, D2, D3, NAIA and JUCO.
3️⃣ Build a mixed list: a few reach schools, mostly good fits.
4️⃣ Email the best-fit coaches first, with video and numbers attached.

Numbers aren't the whole story, and no list guarantees a roster spot. But knowing his level helps him spend his time where coaches are more likely to write back.

Do you know where his numbers stack up?
